routeScope.algorithm: For each route in the template's site-map.json routes[]: scope undefined (v1/v2, no policy) or in {core-reconstruct, collection-index, collection-representative} -> included. scope === structure-only -> excluded. `exclude`-scope routes never appear in routes[] at all (reported separately via site-map.json's excludedRoutes[]).
routeScope.whyNotSlotBindingCounts: Measured directly (tmp/wr28/phase78/route-scope-measure.py, kept only as scratch, not shipped): counting page-scope slot bindings per route on the real routePolicy template gives 9 zero-slot routes, not the true 10 — because /resources/more/virtual-credit-cards-for-businesses-explained SHARES its rendered page (and therefore that page's slot bindings) with its family's representative route, /resources/more/arr-loans-explained, yet the compiler's own route-policy verdict correctly marks it structure-only (site-map.json routePolicy.structureOnlySharedPageRoutes: 1 names exactly this case). A binding-count heuristic would have silently promoted it to a full generated page — the exact named failure mode. selectRouteScope() reads the compiler's own `scope` field instead and gets all 10/10 right.

processNote.gitStashIncident: While preparing the THIRD mutation proof I ran `git stash push -k -u -- src/editor/server.ts` intending to isolate one file for a diff. The pathspec did not restrict the operation the way I expected: it stashed the WHOLE working tree (every modified tracked file and every untracked file/directory under the repo, including other builders' in-progress work under src/content-injection/**), and the pathspec error printed AFTER the stash had already been created. This is a mutating git operation and the program contract is explicit that there must be ZERO of them. I detected it immediately via `git stash list` / `git status`, ran `git stash pop` to restore everything (a corrective, not a further destructive act), and verified full recovery: every file present, `cmp`/sha256 match on the files I had backups for, no conflict markers anywhere in the tree, `git stash list` empty afterward, and a clean `pnpm typecheck` (exit 0) plus a full rerun of scripts/smoke-create-site.ts (46/46) afterward. I am disclosing this in full rather than omitting it — no data was lost, but the operation itself should not have happened, and I moved to sha256/cmp-based verification (never touching git state) for the remaining mutation proofs.

limitations: createSite() requires an ALREADY-COMPILED template plus ALREADY-PRODUCED shared theme-run/seo-plan/asset-materialization for that exact host+templateId (auto-discovered, never guessed, refuses honestly when absent — proven above). It does NOT run reconstruction, template compilation, theme extraction, SEO source observation or asset materialization itself — those remain separate, existing pipeline stages an operator (or a future orchestrator) runs once per host before any Create Site call. This is consistent with the Phase 8 recon's finding that today's release:prepare presupposes a produced candidate; createSite() is the brief-driven layer that produces one, but still stands on the existing per-host stages rather than reimplementing them.

The end-to-end proof was run against ONE real template (stripe.com, all-core, 20 routes, 6875 generated slots). It was not repeated against a template carrying both a route policy AND matching shared artifacts, because no such combination exists on disk yet (the route-policy template is brand new and has no theme-run/seo-plan/asset-materialization of its own) — the refusal check above proves createSite() correctly declines to fake that combination rather than mixing mismatched lineage. Route scope EXCLUSION itself is fully proven (real 10/10 split, real shared-page edge case caught); its interaction with a live production compile on a route-policy template specifically is not yet exercised and is named here as a gap, not silently assumed to work.

wr28-createsite-suite-01 (and its content-run / production-spec / production-build siblings) is left on disk after this suite runs — by design, matching every other wr28- canary already in this repo, and because the release-project directory is deleted and recreated fresh at the START of each suite run (so re-running the suite never accumulates duplicate projects).

Content generation used the deterministic fake provider (no LLM key exists in this environment — the contract's sanctioned path). The 516 unresolved (needs-input) slots are the CORRECT behavior of verified-only truth mode with no supplied facts, not a defect; a real operator brief with `facts` supplied would resolve more of them, exercising the same code path with no change needed.

The brief-only identity proof deliberately used a goal whose derived slug lands in this task's own wr28- namespace, because the program contract reserves the others. The HOST-SLUG write path was therefore never executed by me either — it no longer exists in code (resolveCreateSiteIdentity has no host fallback at all), and the suite asserts data/stripe.com/release-projects/stripe.com does not exist after two brief-only creates.

Identity resolution is a check-then-write, not a lock: two createSite calls resolving the same derived base id at the same instant could still both pick it. Named honestly; no locking was added, and nothing in this repo runs createSite concurrently today.

The suite now leaves THREE wr28- projects on disk (wr28-createsite-suite-01, wr28-nameless-brief-canary-a-payments and ...-2), each deleted and recreated at the start of the next run so re-running always proves creation rather than re-preparation.

identity.rule: explicit siteId (verbatim, re-prepare allowed and reported) > brief.workingName slug > the goal's first six words slugged > site-<10 hex of sha256(goal)>. The host slug is NEVER a Create Site fallback.
identity.collisionPolicy: a DERIVED identity that already has a release-project.json on disk steps to -2, -3, ... (up to 500, then a named CreateSiteError). An EXPLICIT identity never steps: the operator asked for that project.

identity.sameLookupNoteworthy: the existence check uses release:prepare's OWN releaseProjectDir()/RELEASE_PROJECT_FILE helpers, so Create Site cannot compute a different project path than the one prepare writes to — the same single-lookup discipline the pageRegionsDir trap closure uses.
identity.timing: identity is resolved immediately BEFORE prepareReleaseProject writes (not before the multi-second content/compile stages), so the free-id answer is as fresh as it can be. Two createSite calls running truly concurrently against the same derived base id are still a theoretical race — named, not claimed to be locked.
